title: 1 Samuel 28:1–2
context: A short hook: the Philistines prepare for war with Israel, and Achish expects David to march with him. David gives an ambiguous answer, and Achish makes him his bodyguard. The story then turns to Saul before resolving David’s dilemma.

verses.text: In those days, the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. Achish said to David, “Know assuredly that you will go out with me in the army, you and your men.”
verses.arminianNotes: As the Philistines gather for war against Israel, Achish says, “Know assuredly that you will go out with me in the army.” Arminian readers see David trapped by the arrangement he chose.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the crisis created by David’s position among the Philistines. The hook raises a pressing question: will the anointed future king fight against his own people?

verses.text: David said to Achish, “Therefore you will know what your servant can do.” Achish said to David, “Therefore I will make you my bodyguard forever.”
verses.arminianNotes: David answers, “Therefore you will know what your servant can do,” and Achish makes him his bodyguard. Arminian readers see an evasive reply that keeps David’s real intentions hidden.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see ambiguity in David’s words. The narrator leaves the outcome suspended and turns to Saul, so the resolution of David’s dilemma waits until chapter 29.
